Ever wonder why a bore wall doesn't cave in straight away?
Mix bentonite with water and it breaks apart into thousands of tiny flat flakes, floating loose in the fluid instead of sitting as a lump of mud.

As that fluid moves past raw ground, those flakes plate out against the wall in thin layers, building a skin over the exposed earth.

That skin is what stops the hole drinking water and caving in once your string's through.

Same clay, same water, different job to the one most drillers know bentonite for, this one's about sealing the wall, not lifting cuttings.
Ever had a bore go from stable to caving in the moment the mud thinned out?

HDD Gel is one bentonite, four different jobs.
HDD Gel's the sodium bentonite doing the wall-sealing job from Wednesday's post. Mix it in and it holds the bore open across HDD, tunnelling, waterwell and piling work.

It's the quicker, simpler bentonite in the range to mix, built for standard ground, not the toughest bores.

Don't swap it out, build on it. Add Carry Flow for the polymer side, Filter Low or Filter High when the ground's porous, Torque Down on the long pulls.

Long bores in tough ground call for Max Gel or Max Bore instead. Everywhere else, HDD Gel's the one product that covers the shed.
Which of those four disciplines is your crew running this week?
